newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World inflation outlook positive - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: World inflation outlook positive - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said central bank governors from the Group of 10 (G10) industralised countries believed that the inflationary environment was currently positive on a global scale.
Tietmeyer, speaking as chairman of the G10 central bankers committee, also said world economic growth looked favourable, especially in the United States.
Economic growth was also progressing in Japan, Britain, the Netherlands, Germany and to some extent in France, he told reporters.
Tietmeyer was speaking after individual central bank governors briefed the committee on developments in their countries at their monthly meeting at the Basle-based Bank for International Settlements.
"Monetary authorities have always to be vigilant, but for the time being it seems to be the case that the inflationary situation all in all is a positive one," Tietmeyer said.
"I am talking about worldwide," he added, declining to be specific when asked about inflationary prospects in the United States.
Tietmeyer said the committee's discussions included a presentation on U.S. economic prospects by Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan.

Referring to global economic growth prospects, he said: "All in all we see that the current trends are mostly favourable. This is especially the case in the United States...the short-term outlook seems to be favourable."
He said Japan was benefitting from improving consumer confidence and spending supported by an improved labour market.
"In Japan, the upward trend is continuing," he also said.
